editorial:
Imagine a grumpy millionaire from the 1920s who decides to play a giant prank on his own family. You get to follow a wealthy man who pretends he has lost his mind or his memory just to see which of his relatives actually care about him and who is just after his money. It is a lighthearted comedy set in a cozy Vermont town, and the vibe feels like a warm hug. You will spend most of the time laughing at the chaos he causes and rooting for the young couple who get caught up in his weird little game. 

The acting is top-notch for its time, and the pacing keeps you moving along without any boring spots. While some of the jokes might feel a bit old-fashioned, the charm of the story makes up for it. If you enjoy old-school humor and sweet romances, you will love this one. Since it is an older film, you might want to look for a high-quality version. If you can find it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, go for it, or maybe rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. Adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is also a great move if you love classic cinema.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up when the millionaire finally reveals that his strange behavior was all a test. He admits he was just checking to see if his family truly loved him or only wanted his wealth. Once the truth comes out, the tension disappears and everyone learns a lesson about greed. The young couple gets their happy ending, and the family makes peace, proving that love is more valuable than a bank account.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old-fashioned comedies and family dramas.
